program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 1500

source_provenance: collision screening against merged history, pending Waves 501-1000, and active Waves 1001-1325

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 1500

waves.focus: Large COSMOS secondary analysis found daily multivitamin-multimineral supplementation did not reduce incident hypertension or two-year blood-pressure change overall; diet-quality and baseline-BP subgroup signals were exploratory and directionally inconsistent.

Systematic review of 43 clinical studies found the vitamin-E/cognition literature was dominated by dietary exposure and multivitamin studies, with very little isolated-supplement evidence; apparent protective associations may reflect dietary or multi-component synergy rather than vitamin E alone.

Four-week double-blind RCT in 155 adults with vitamin A, D or E deficiency found nutrition education plus multivitamin was not superior to nutrition education plus placebo for improving vitamin concentrations or deficiency rates; both groups improved substantially.

Two-year COSMOS biomarker substudy found multivitamin supplementation increased total carotenoids, lutein, beta-carotene and alpha-tocopherol concentrations, while several other carotenoids were unchanged; this demonstrates exposure/biomarker effects rather than clinical benefit.

Large COSMOS ancillary analysis found neither cocoa extract nor multivitamin-multimineral supplementation significantly reduced venous thromboembolism, DVT or pulmonary embolism in intention-to-treat analyses; per-protocol and latency patterns were exploratory.

Prespecified COSMOS ancillary study found small two-year changes favoring multivitamin supplementation on PCGrimAge and PCPhenoAge epigenetic clocks, while cocoa extract was null; effect sizes were small and clinical relevance remains uncertain.

COSMOS metabolomics substudy found nominal multivitamin-associated changes in DHA, omega-3, creatinine and multiple disease-risk scores, but none survived false-discovery-rate correction; findings are preliminary rather than validated metabolic benefits.

Twenty-four-week randomized prenatal trial found 6S-5-MTHF maintained total maternal/fetal folate similarly to folic acid while producing less detectable unmetabolized folic acid in maternal blood and placenta; clinical developmental superiority was not tested.

COSMOS clinic substudy found neither cocoa extract nor multivitamin supplementation improved two-year grip strength, walking speed, SPPB, balance, chair-stand or timed-up-and-go outcomes in older adults.

Single-blind randomized comparison found organically sourced and synthetic multivitamin-mineral formulations produced broadly comparable acute and 30-day circulating micronutrient profiles, providing no evidence of general bioavailability superiority for the organic formulation.

COSMOS secondary analysis found daily multivitamin supplementation did not significantly reduce COVID-19 incidence in intention-to-treat analysis; a symptomatic-COVID signal appeared only in adherent per-protocol analysis and remains secondary.

Twenty-four-week double-blind prenatal trial found a higher-biotin multivitamin increased maternal and cord-blood biotin biomarkers and reduced a marginal-insufficiency metabolite; cortisol associations were exploratory and no maternal or infant clinical benefit was established.

Exploratory systematic review/meta-analysis found highly heterogeneous psychiatric evidence for vitamin D and B12; vitamin-D signals attenuated toward null after bias adjustment and B12 supplementation evidence was sparse/null, supporting targeted deficiency assessment rather than routine supplementation.

Small double-blind placebo-controlled trial in 40 gynecologic-cancer patients found oral vitamin B12 reduced the incidence of questionnaire-defined chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, while neurotoxicity quality-of-life scores and adverse effects did not differ; replication is needed.

Tiny randomized crossover dental-surgery pilot replacing nighttime ibuprofen with melatonin, vitamin D and B12 did not improve overall recovery and produced higher pain/swelling on several measures; sex-interaction findings were exploratory and the multi-ingredient design prevents attribution.

Systematic review associated excessive folic-acid intake or high blood folate during preconception/pregnancy with gestational diabetes and selected offspring/growth outcomes, but evidence was heterogeneous and largely association-based; it does not establish a causal toxic threshold.

Randomized trial in 153 adults with B12-deficiency anemia found intranasal, intravenous and intramuscular B12 all produced short-term hematologic recovery, with no significant adjusted difference in hemoglobin response by route; some secondary laboratory kinetics differed.

Six-month double-blind community RCT in 472 Ethiopian teenage girls found B9/B12-fortified corn flour did not improve any primary cognitive outcome versus unfortified flour; a stunting-language interaction was secondary and not evidence of benefit.

One-month double-blind trial in a mostly female general-population sample found 100 mg/day vitamin B6 reduced depression scores only in preselected participants with elevated baseline symptoms, with no anxiety or stress benefit; subgroup design and high dose require cautious safety-aware interpretation.

Exploratory randomized rheumatology trial found increasing folic acid from 5 to 10 mg/week did not meaningfully reduce methotrexate-related liver or other toxicity over 12 weeks; a fatigue difference was isolated and secondary.

Randomized trial in 248 anemic children found adding Lactobacillus plantarum to iron-folic-acid therapy provided no additional benefit for hemoglobin, iron status, morbidity, adverse effects or gut-health markers versus iron-folic acid alone.

Large double-blind noninferiority trial in Bangladeshi women with iron-deficiency anemia found both tested bovine-lactoferrin doses were inferior to ferrous sulfate for 12-week hemoglobin recovery, with similar adverse-event rates.

Randomized pregnancy substudy in Ghana found multiple-micronutrient supplementation containing zinc did not significantly improve late-pregnancy plasma zinc or zinc-deficiency prevalence versus iron-folic acid; zinc status worsened across pregnancy in both groups.

Double-blind trial in couples with recurrent pregnancy loss found alpha-lipoic acid plus folic acid reduced sperm DNA-fragmentation index versus folic-acid control, while between-group sperm concentration, motility and morphology differences were not significant; fertility/live-birth benefit was not established.

Double-blind RCT in 110 pregnant women found equimolar 5-MTHF and folic acid produced comparable RBC-folate gains and homocysteine reductions; plasma 5-MTHF and unmetabolized-folate differences were borderline or nonsignificant after adjustment.
